record.paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
record.context_brief: Mass-loss law for RGB and AGB stars
record.original_question: How can stellar evolution theory determine a physically grounded and empirically calibrated description of mass loss during the Red Giant Branch and Asymptotic Giant Branch stages for Population II giants, including the mass-loss timescales, the mechanisms that drive the mass loss, and how the efficiency depends on stellar parameters and metallicity, so that stellar model computations no longer rely on poorly justified extrapolations of prescriptions calibrated on Population I bright giants?

evidence.quote: However, despite its importance, complete empirical determinations as well as a comprehensive physical description of the involved processes are still lacking.

From a theoretical point of view, our knowledge of the ML timescales, driving mechanisms, dependence on stellar parameters and metallicity is also very poor. The consequence is that there is little theoretical or observational guidance on how to incorporate ML into stellar model computations.

artifact.category_tag: stellar mass loss on RGB and AGB
artifact.status_search_result: Mass loss on the RGB and AGB of Population II giants remains an active area of research without a consensus, physically grounded prescription. Recent works continue to propose and test new empirical and semi-empirical formulae (e.g., Schröder–Cuntz, Origlia et al. observations with Spitzer, MIST/PARSEC isochrone calibrations), but a complete physical theory tying mass-loss rates to stellar parameters and metallicity for low-metallicity giants is still lacking. The problem is therefore open.

status_evidence.title: Mass loss of Population II red giants — review discussions
status_evidence.snippet: complete empirical determinations as well as a comprehensive physical description of the involved processes are still lacking
status_evidence.claim: As of the source, the physical/empirical description of RGB/AGB mass loss in Pop II giants is incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Origlia et al., Spitzer observations of mass loss on the RGB
status_evidence.snippet: empirical mass-loss law calibrated on globular cluster red giants suggests episodic, low-rate dust-driven winds
status_evidence.claim: Empirical constraints have been refined but no first-principles theory yet exists.

status_evidence.title: Reviews of AGB mass loss (Höfner & Olofsson 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: mass loss mechanisms and their metallicity dependence remain only partially understood
status_evidence.claim: Driving mechanisms and metallicity dependence of AGB mass loss are still under investigation.
